INVESTMENT RECOMMENDATION: COST (fiscal year ended 2026-08-30)

Rating: Hold

Thesis: The business and the financials agree. Costco is growing with solid demand, funds that growth from its own cash flow, and has low leverage. The supplied valuation leaves little margin for error. The price is user-supplied with an unverified date, and no peer P/E exists to show the premium is justified. I would hold the position and not add to it.

Source limits: The Research Analyst could not use the 10-K Business and MD&A sections ("10-K.txt: Item 1 section was not found." and "10-K.txt: Item 7 section was not found."). Competitive advantage, member counts, renewal rates, opening plans and segment profitability are therefore "not stated in the files." The Financial Analyst drew no peer valuation conclusion.

Where the analysts agree:
- Growth is real and broad. Net sales rose 10.1% to $297.2 billion [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L10]. Adjusted 52-week total company comparable sales were 6.6% [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37].
- Growth is funded internally. Capex was 6,435,000,000 [XBRL tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]. Free cash flow was 9,382,000,000 (computed, rechecked given calculations: 15817000000 - 6435000000), from operating cash flow of 15,817,000,000 [XBRL tag NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093].
- Leverage is low. Debt to equity was 0.17210848252939698 (computed, rechecked given calculations) [XBRL tags LongTermDebtNoncurrent, LongTermDebtCurrent and StockholdersEquity, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093].

Where they differ:
- The release shows operating cash flow of 15,825 [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L306], while the XBRL tag shows 15,817,000,000. I rely on the XBRL figure used in the free cash flow calculation. The gap is small and does not change the conclusion.
- The Research Analyst says the one-time tariff refund makes underlying earnings growth somewhat lower than the headline. The Financial Analyst computes the $0.15 benefit as 0.722543352601156% of fiscal-year diluted EPS (computed, rechecked given calculations) [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44; XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]. I treat the item as too small to drive the thesis. Its direction is still a caution against extrapolating the fourth quarter.

Criteria:
1. Thesis support: SUPPORTED. Sales growth and rising membership fees (5,907 vs 5,323, [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L81-L82]) match the profit and cash results. Operating income was 11,685,000,000 vs 10,383,000,000 [XBRL tag OperatingIncomeLoss, period ends 2026-08-30 and 2025-08-31]. Return on average equity was 28.402111841396398% (computed, rechecked given calculations) [XBRL tags NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity]. The limits are a thin operating margin of 3.8544766026507977% (computed, rechecked given calculations) [XBRL tags OperatingIncomeLoss and RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, period end 2026-08-30], and no competitor evidence, because the Research Analyst rated competitive position MIXED.
2. Downside exposure: MIXED. The current portion of long-term debt rose to 2,248,000,000 from 75,000,000 [XBRL tag LongTermDebtCurrent, period ends 2026-08-30 and 2025-08-31]. Cash and cash equivalents of 20,207 [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L177] and free cash flow of 9,382,000,000 cover that maturity, so the weakness does not undermine the thesis now. Rising capex is the pressure point: 6,435,000,000 vs 5,498,000,000 [XBRL tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment]. Prior-year free cash flow and ShortTermBorrowings are not available, because ShortTermBorrowings is "not stated in the files."
3. Valuation support: MIXED. P/E was 47.79046242774566 (computed, rechecked given calculations: 992.13 / 20.76) [XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]. The price is user-supplied at run time 2026-11-05T08:45:47-05:00 and its date is unverified. Peer P/E is "not stated in the files." Peer fiscal periods end 2026-01-31, not 2026-08-30, so no peer comparison is possible. This evidence does not support a Buy.

Deciding number: P/E of 47.79046242774566 (computed, rechecked given calculations: 992.13 / 20.76) [XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]. It carries the most weight because the business and funding evidence is already favorable. The remaining question is whether that quality is priced in, and a very high multiple on an unverified price leaves no demonstrated cushion.

Main risk: At that multiple, any slowdown in capex-funded growth would hurt, while 2,248,000,000 of debt is now current [XBRL tag LongTermDebtCurrent, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]. A fall in free cash flow would weaken the internal-funding support for that multiple.

What would change the rating: If the next filing reports annual free cash flow below 9,382,000,000 (computed, rechecked given calculations: 15817000000 - 6435000000) [XBRL tags NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities and PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, filing 0000909832-26-000093] because capex keeps rising faster than operating cash flow, I would move from Hold toward Sell. A filing cannot justify a Buy on its own, because the valuation concern would still need a verified price and peer P/E evidence.

Insight: At a P/E of 47.79046242774566, Costco's valuation depends on its internally funded growth continuing, and that growth produced free cash flow of 9,382,000,000 after 6,435,000,000 of capital spending.
